messages:
nina: Quick heads-up — ran a replay of last week's tail session against the new kernel-selection heuristic branch. p95 looks OK, but p99 has spikes when microbatch_size=4 on q4_0 kernels (A100). Not sure if this is an artifact of the replay or a real regression.

mike: Can you paste the run config and a tiny log snip?

nina: Sure — config used: 
```
microbatch_size: 4
concurrency_per_gpu: 16
kernel_strategy: \"auto\"
quant: \"q4_0\"
kv_cache: \"lru_prefix\"
sequence_lengths: replayed
```
Log snippet: 
```
[14:03:21] request_id=abc123 latency=512ms model_step=34 kernel=matmul_v2
[14:03:22] request_id=def456 latency=820ms model_step=12 kernel=matmul_v2
p99 window: ~800ms for top 0.7% of samples
```

charlie: Interesting. Microbatch=4 is our common sweet spot for throughput but it's small enough that kernel selection noise can show up. Could be queuing jitter + kernel choice thrash.

tara: Replay can exaggerate tails if client inter-arrival times are clumped — did you preserve original timestamps or replay with fixed inter-arrival?

nina: preserved timestamps. Replayer did not inject additional pacing.

kai: If timestamps are preserved we get burstiness from the original traffic. That can push the runtime to use different kernels (short vs long-path kernels) between microbatches. Auto kernel chooser oscillates.

sam: perf-bot flagged a p99 delta: \"perf-bot: ALERT: p99 increased 8.2% vs baseline (baseline: 310ms, test: 335ms), run_id=1951234567\"

mike: Oof. 8% is small but meaningful at our SLOs. Do we see the same with synthetic loadgen?

nina: Ran a synthetic run yesterday with Poisson arrivals and constant seq len. p99 was flat, no spike. So replay shows problem, synth does not. :thinking: 

charlie: Classic. Synthetic loadgen smooths inter-arrival tails and often hides kernel handoff effects. Replay preserves real-world burstiness + cold-KV hits.

tara: Also check KV cache warmup. If replay includes sessions that hit cold prefixes, kv misses will force longer execution and different kernel paths. We should stratify by whether KV hit or miss.

kai: Agree. Proposal: 1) run replay but tag requests by kv_hit true/false; 2) run a hybrid loadgen that replays arrival times but scrambles user prefixes so kv misses are randomized; 3) run microbatch sweep {2,4,8} with kernel pinning toggled.

sam: I'll ask perf-bot to compare runs automatically. perf-bot: please run compare against baseline-1950000000 and output p95/p99 per-kernel and kv-hit breakdown.

perf-bot: Ack — scheduling diff job. Expect CSV + small flamegraph in ~45m.

mike: Also log kernel selection transitions. Even if p99 is ok on synth, transitions under burst can cause short bursts of heavy matmuls. We need per-request kernel id in traces.

charlie: Note: lowering microbatch to 2 eliminated the p99 spike locally but reduced throughput ~18% in our bench. So it's a throughput vs tail tradeoff.

nina: Right. We need to quantify cost impact if product teams require microbatch=2 to meet SLOs. That affects unit economics.

tara: I'll run the hybrid plan tomorrow and add KV-hit tagging. I'll also include a run that pins kernel_strategy=prefer_short to see if that stabilizes tail.

kai: If kernel pinning helps, maybe we can add a short window sticky policy: once a kernel is picked for a model shard, keep it for N seconds unless latency degrades. Might reduce oscillation.

sam: Agree — for rollout we could try canary with sticky-kernel enabled on 5% of traffic and monitor p99 and throughput.

nina: Action list: @tara run hybrid replay + synth tomorrow and post CSVs; @sam have perf-bot run the delta and flamegraphs; @mike/charlie investigate sticky-kernel policy feasibility and estimate perf cost; everyone drop short notes into #eng-runtime/bench-logs.

mike: +1. Also let's add a measurement note: always publish p95 & p99 with the sampling window and concurrency distribution. Without that metadata, comparisons are meaningless.

charlie: And annotate whether replays preserved client pacing or normalized it.

nina: Cool — thanks. If the perf-bot diff shows kernel-specific p99 hits we can file a regression ticket and consider a micropatch (sticky kernel or kv-prefetch). Thanks all :thumbsup:
